Model approach determined by HAZARD_MODEL_DECISIONS.csv HMD01. Recommended approach: Multi-criteria index model combining terrain, hydrology, and observed flood drivers. Inputs and indicative weights (to be approved — see HMD01): (1) Flow accumulation G14 — drainage concentration; (2) Slope G10 — terrain gradient; (3) Distance to rivers G05 — proximity to flood source; (4) Annual rainfall G22 — precipitation driver; (5) Land cover G15 — runoff/infiltration modifier; (6) Observed flood locations G25 — calibration/validation. Processing steps: Step 1: Confirm all upstream layers are CLEAN. Step 2: Normalise each input to 0-100 scale. Step 3: Apply approved weights (HMD01). Step 4: Compute weighted sum to produce continuous hazard index raster (0-100). Step 5: Classify into hazard zones (Very Low / Low / Moderate / High / Very High) using approved thresholds (HMD02). Step 6: Validate classified zones against G25 observed flood locations. Step 7: Publish CLEAN raster and derived hazard zone polygons.

CRITICAL: Input weights and classification thresholds must be pre-specified in HAZARD_MODEL_DECISIONS.csv (HMD01 and HMD02) BEFORE computation begins. They MUST NOT be changed after seeing the output. G24 is a decision-support hazard INDEX — it is not a flood return period map and must not be described as a probability of flooding. Every G24 output must carry its model version (Risk_Model_Version) and input layer versions in metadata. G25 observed floods are used for VALIDATION only — not as an additional input weight (this would create circular validation). Sensitivity analysis with alternate input weights is recommended and must be pre-specified (see HMD01).
